items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Because those are my lyrics to “Milestones.”

ctx.x: I love it. Tell me about your creative process. This, for those who are watching, this is “Miles Tones.” This is your most recent one, right?

Um hum. Well I have to like the melody. I have to like the melody. Because those are my lyrics to “Milestones.” And I have to like the melody. Because it’s got to be lyrical. It’s got to be singable. It’s got to be hummable. So if I like the melody enough, and I listen to it enough, and then I go by the title. I refer to the title. Right? What’s this about. Well it’s about milestones. What are milestones? Yardsticks? Meters? Inches? Measurement. Can you measure life? And you live with it for a while. The melody.…
You know that song has a thing that I wonder, the A section is very up, and then the bridge is much more flowing.

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Miles Davis, you know, Miles Davis didn’t do an act, but people came to see what he was going to do next.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well it’s hard to teach somebody something that you don’t know about. I mean they don’t know about it. They don’t know about maybe getting kicked off the bandstand.

You know? “Nice try baby, come back another time.” So that’ll either make you quit or go home and work on it. Or you know I went to watch before I ever tried to do this, I was a fan. So I saw Joe Williams sing a lot of times. And I wasn’t just listening to him sing, I would watch the way he would get up from the stool. I mean you do something a little different when you’re on stage, because they realized that yeah you’re listening to me but you’re also looking at me. So you have to present yourself in a certain…
